low: Drawing ability: LOW, the earliest preschool scribble stage, with almost no drawing control. Begin from a blank sheet and reconstruct only the largest impressions of the source. Make a sparse, awkward, barely detailed drawing with a blunt wax crayon. Core visual elements: a few badly proportioned primitive lumps and only two or three crude identifying marks. Use wandering open contours and clumsy disconnected joins. Smooth small contour changes into large lopsided lumps. Supporting content: collapse nearby small forms into broad uneven color patches. Background, when present: show only its rough color placement as continuous smears with vague, rounded, irregular boundaries and empty interiors. Combine dense or distant small forms into broad uneven masses. Coarse recognizable silhouettes and changes in height are acceptable when their interiors remain empty or loosely scribbled. Use flat scribbled color, visible white gaps and uncontrolled overshoots. Reserve recognizability for the core visual structure, grouping and arrangement. Incidental inscriptions become one to three loose nonalphabetic strokes or blank areas; omit all spelling, readable fragments, digits and copied character shapes. LOW fails if the background contains precise contours, fine internal structure or regular small details, if shading suggests skilled construction, or if incidental text is readable. Keep clear paper and wax grain at normal output resolution. Apply explicit user exceptions only to their specified content.
medium: Drawing ability: MEDIUM, the default. Build recognizable visual elements from simple, uneven shapes with a few approximate identifying features. Detail accuracy, completeness and hand control are intermediate: retain basic structure, use hesitant or disconnected short contours, and leave some minor parts incomplete. Supporting objects have rough silhouettes and a small number of key interior marks. Where a background exists, distinguish its main groups using broad flat patches and occasional coarse structural marks; dense or distant groups remain simplified. Incidental inscriptions become broken, loosely letter-like marks with little legible content. Use broad patchy fills and a few rough overlapping color areas for depth. Keep visibly less detail, precision and completeness than HIGH and more recognizable structure than LOW. Preserve the core visual structure, grouping, arrangement and source colors.
high: Drawing ability: HIGH. Produce a practiced child's wax-crayon drawing with the most recognizable detail of the three levels. Build visual elements from awkward elementary shapes, uneven contours and broad patchy fills. Preserve more characteristic internal features, secondary object structure and coarse shading patches than MEDIUM. Where a background exists, its major objects remain separately recognizable with simplified internal features. Existing incidental lettering may remain recognizable with uneven hand-drawn strokes. Local exaggeration, asymmetry, sparse scribbles and imperfect joins keep the construction visibly childlike at thumbnail size. Preserve the core visual structure, grouping, arrangement and source colors.
